advances:
In the first unresolved target-rank-two and heaviest-label-residual-rank-two hard \(I\)-subcase, every translate of the actual residual section \(B_*/2\) carries at most \(G\) canonical \(I\)-triangle target mass. More generally, a union of \(N\) such translates carries at most \(NG\). Consequently, a cover of the full residual support by at most
\[
 \left\lfloor\frac{3}{1-2(d/(d+1))^d}\right\rfloor
\]
translates is terminal after adding the distinct numerical summands \(G\), \(R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)\), and \(D=2^nh_{\max}(C)\). No upper bound on the residual-cell cover number is asserted.

proof:
Fix \(c\in\mathcal T\). There are at most \(2^n\) parity labels at the physical target \(c\), so the maximizing choice in (8) gives
\[
 \widehat\theta_c\ge2^{-n}T_c.
\tag{17}
\]
Equation (2) gives
\[
 0<\widehat\theta_c\le\frac12S_{\xi(c),c}.
\tag{18}
\]
Accepted fact 07889c9b4686d8b4 gives the separate, single-label estimate
\[
 \widehat\theta_c\le\frac{a_c}{16}.
\tag{19}
\]
In particular, \(c\in Z\), and no masses or representing densities belonging to different parity labels have been pooled.

Put
\[
 m_c:=4\widehat\theta_c.
\tag{20}
\]
Equations (18) and (19) imply
\[
 0<m_c\le2S_{\xi(c),c},\qquad
 m_c\le\frac{a_c}{4}.
\tag{21}
\]
We claim that the full translated set in (5), not only its center, remains available at mass \(m_c\):
\[
 q_c+\frac12D_*\subseteq\mathsf M_{m_c}(C_c).
\tag{22}
\]
Indeed, fix \(y\in q_c+D_*/2\). By (5), there is a density \(f_y\) on \(C_c\) with \(0\le f_y\le1\), total mass \(2S_{\xi(c),c}\), and normalized barycenter \(y\). Multiplying \(f_y\) by \(m_c/(2S_{\xi(c),c})\le1\) gives an admissible density of mass \(m_c\) with the same normalized barycenter. This proves (22) pointwise, using only the one selected label at \(c\).

Fix \(w\in V\), and let
\[
 E_w:=\left\{c\in\mathcal T:u_c\in w+\frac12B_*\right\}.
\tag{23}
\]
If \(E_w=\varnothing\), then (12) is immediate. Assume \(E_w\ne\varnothing\), and put
\[
 \tau_w:=\sum_{c\in E_w}m_c.
\tag{24}
\]
For \(c\in E_w\), the origin symmetry of \(B_*\) gives
\[
 w-u_c\in\frac12B_*\subseteq\frac12D_*.
\]
Therefore (10) and (22) give
\[
 s(c)+w=q_c+(w-u_c)\in\mathsf M_{m_c}(C_c).
\tag{25}
\]
Thus one affine map on the target plane supplies one actual metronoid point in each distinct physical target fiber of \(E_w\).

Let
\[
 B:=\operatorname{aff}(E_w),\qquad q:=\dim B\le2.
\]
The weighted lattice centerpoint theorem in accepted fact 6d6fcf377e68c79c, transported through an affine lattice isomorphism from \(B\cap\mathbb Z^n\) to \(\mathbb Z^q\), supplies
\[
 b\in B\cap\mathbb Z^n\cap\operatorname{conv}(E_w)
\tag{26}
\]
such that every proper relative closed halfspace of \(B\) containing \(b\) carries at least \(2^{-q}\tau_w\) of the atomic weights \(m_c\). For completeness, after choosing \(b_0\in E_w\), the group
\[
 \Gamma:=(B-b_0)\cap\mathbb Z^n
\]
has rank \(q\), and a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis of \(\Gamma\) maps \(\mathbb Z^q\) bijectively onto \(B\cap\mathbb Z^n\). Applying the \(d=0\) specialization of accepted fact 6d6fcf377e68c79c to the pushforward weights gives the centerpoint. If the selected point lay outside \(\operatorname{conv}(E_w)\), a separating halfspace containing it would carry zero mass, proving the final inclusion in (26).

The trace on \(B\) of a proper relative closed halfspace of \(A\) containing \(b\) is either all of \(B\) or a proper relative closed halfspace of \(B\) containing \(b\). Since \(q\le2\), every such halfspace of \(A\) carries at least
\[
 2^{-q}\tau_w\ge\frac14\tau_w.
\tag{27}
\]
For every barycentric representation
\[
 \lambda\in\Lambda_b(E_w)
 :=\left\{\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^{E_w}:
 \sum_c\lambda_c=1,\ \sum_c\lambda_cc=b\right\},
\]
affinity of \(s\) and (25) give
\[
 s(b)+w
 =\sum_{c\in E_w}\lambda_c(s(c)+w)
 \in\sum_{c\in E_w}\lambda_c\mathsf M_{m_c}(C_c).
\tag{28}
\]
The left side is independent of \(\lambda\), so the complete metronoid core is nonempty.

We now pass from this rank-two relative witness to the global capacity, treating the full-rank case separately. If \(n=2\), then (7) forces \(A=\mathbb R^2\). Equations (21), (27), and (28) make the tuple \((m_c)_{c\in E_w}\) directly admissible for the global capacity \(G\), because the relative balance \(1/4\) is exactly the ambient balance \(2^{-n}\). Hence
\[
 G\ge\tau_w=2^{n-2}\tau_w.
\tag{29}
\]

Suppose \(n>2\), so \(A\subsetneq\mathbb R^n\). Equations (21), (27), and (28) make the tuple admissible for the relative complete-core capacity \(G_A^{\mathrm{rel}}\) in accepted fact 3d1f63abf09b2abb, and therefore
\[
 G_A^{\mathrm{rel}}\ge\tau_w.
\tag{30}
\]
Put
\[
 W_A:=\sum_{z\in Z\cap A}a_z.
\tag{31}
\]
The full target support \(\mathcal T\subseteq Z\cap A\) spans \(A\), so
\[
 \dim\operatorname{aff}(Z\cap A)=2.
\]
Accepted fact 8aac56c49321466c applied to this actual occupied-fiber slice gives
\[
 G\ge\frac1{64}\min\{W,2^{n-2}W_A\}.
\tag{32}
\]
The hard inequality (1), together with \(Q\le W/8\) from accepted fact 7ec63df101c30343, gives
\[
 G<\frac Q{100}\le\frac W{800}.
\tag{33}
\]
Since \(W_A>0\), (32) also shows \(G>0\). Equations (32) and (33) rule out \(W\) as the minimum in (32), and hence
\[
 2^{n-2}W_A\le64G,\qquad
 W_A\le32G
 \quad(n\ge3).
\tag{34}
\]
Together with \(W>800G\), this yields
\[
 \frac{W-W_A}{2}>384G>G.
\tag{35}
\]
The one-sided augmentation theorem 3d1f63abf09b2abb gives
\[
 G\ge
 \min\left\{
 G_A^{\mathrm{rel}}+\frac{W-W_A}{2},
 2^{n-2}G_A^{\mathrm{rel}}
 \right\}.
\tag{36}
\]
The first entry in (36) is greater than \(G\) by (35). Therefore the second entry is at most \(G\). Combining this with (30) gives
\[
 G\ge2^{n-2}\tau_w.
\tag{37}
\]
Equations (29) and (37) prove (37) for every \(n\ge2\).

Finally, (17), (20), and (24) give
\[
 \tau_w
 =4\sum_{c\in E_w}\widehat\theta_c
 \ge4\cdot2^{-n}\sum_{c\in E_w}T_c.
\tag{38}
\]
Multiplying (38) by \(2^{n-2}\) and using (37) proves
\[
 G\ge\sum_{c\in E_w}T_c
 =\mu_I\!\left(w+\frac12B_*\right),
\]
which is (12). Subadditivity of \(\mu_I\) proves (13). If (14) holds, then (13) and \(\mu_I(V)=\Theta_I\) give \(G\ge\Theta_I/N\).

Apply accepted fact e2263a787ace07a4 to the full target support \(\mathcal T\). Its target rank is \(2\), and its fixed heaviest-label residual rank is \(2\), so that accepted theorem gives
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)\ge\frac{\gamma_d}{3}\Theta_I,
 \qquad
 D\ge R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C).
\tag{39}
\]
Accepted fact e2263a787ace07a4 also audits that \(R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)\) and \(D\) are distinct nonnegative numerical summands of \(\mathcal A(C)\). Their witnesses need not be disjoint. Under (14), equations (13) and (39) therefore give
\[
 \mathcal A(C)
 \ge G+R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)+D
 \ge\left(\frac1N+\frac{2\gamma_d}{3}\right)\Theta_I.
\tag{40}
\]
Since \(d\ge2\), the binomial expansion gives
\[
 \left(1+\frac1d\right)^d
 \ge1+1+\frac{d-1}{2d}>2,
\]
so \(0<\gamma_d<1/2\). Put
\[
 \kappa_d:=\frac{1-2\gamma_d}{3}>0.
\]
For an integer \(N\ge1\),
\[
 \frac1N+\frac{2\gamma_d}{3}\ge\frac13
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 N\le\frac1{\kappa_d}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 N\le N_d.
\tag{41}
\]
Thus (40), (41), and the strict bound \(\Theta_I>3Q/100\) prove (16). Conversely, if \(N>N_d\), the coefficient supplied by this particular three-summand estimate is strictly below \(1/3\). This proves the asserted exactness of the integer threshold without claiming that a larger cover is nonterminal by some other mechanism.

The proof uses only the physical target plane \(A\), its selected target-fiber points, and the actual section \(B_*=D_*\cap V\). It never identifies \(A\) with a source triangle chart and never combines two parity-label densities in one target fiber.
statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and assume the canonical hard \(I\)-branch of accepted facts 6b09aae189415c70 and 7ec63df101c30343. Use their notation
\[
 a_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),\qquad
 Z:=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:a_z>0\},\qquad
 W:=\sum_{z\in Z}a_z,
\]
\[
 G:=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{core}}(C),\qquad
 D:=2^nh_{\max}(C),
\]
and
\[
 \mathcal A(C):=R+G+R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)+M_{\mathrm{off}}(C)
 +R_{\mathrm{cloud}}(C)+D<\frac Q{100}.
\tag{1}
\]
In particular, \(n\ge2\), \(Q\le W/8\), and the actual transverse triangle construction of accepted fact 7ec63df101c30343 has \(I\)-bad opposite-edge masses \(t_e\) with
\[
 0\le t_e\le\frac12s_e.
\tag{2}
\]
For every retained parity label \((\xi,c)\), put
\[
 S_{\xi,c}:=\sum_{\substack{e\subseteq\xi\\m_e=c}}s_e,
 \qquad
 \Theta_{\xi,c}:=
 \sum_{\substack{e\subseteq\xi,\ m_e=c\\e\in\mathcal E_I}}t_e,
\tag{3}
\]
and use the actual conditioned-output point \(q_{\xi,c}^{\circ}\) and the common origin-symmetric full-dimensional body \(D_*\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) from accepted fact 6b09aae189415c70. For \(0<m\le\operatorname{vol}_d(K)\), write
\[
 \mathsf M_m(K):=
 \left\{\frac1m\int_Kx f(x)\,dx:
 0\le f\le1\ {\rm a.e.},\quad \int_Kf=m\right\}.
\tag{4}
\]
The accepted conditioned-output inclusion is
\[
 q_{\xi,c}^{\circ}+\frac12D_*
 \subseteq \mathsf M_{2S_{\xi,c}}(C_c)
 \qquad(S_{\xi,c}>0).
\tag{5}
\]
Define
\[
 T_c:=\sum_\xi\Theta_{\xi,c},\qquad
 \mathcal T:=\{c\in\mathbb Z^n:T_c>0\},\qquad
 \Theta_I:=\sum_{c\in\mathcal T}T_c.
\tag{6}
\]
Then \(\Theta_I>3Q/100\). Assume
\[
 A:=\operatorname{aff}(\mathcal T),\qquad \dim A=2.
\tag{7}
\]
For every \(c\in\mathcal T\), choose one retained parity label \(\xi(c)\) maximizing \(\Theta_{\xi,c}\), and set
\[
 \widehat\theta_c:=\Theta_{\xi(c),c},\qquad
 q_c:=q_{\xi(c),c}^{\circ}.
\tag{8}
\]
Assume that these fixed heaviest-label points have continuous residual rank exactly two:
\[
 \min_{s:A\to\mathbb R^d\ \mathrm{affine}}
 \dim\operatorname{span}\{q_c-s(c):c\in\mathcal T\}=2.
\tag{9}
\]
Choose any affine map \(s\) attaining this minimum and put
\[
 u_c:=q_c-s(c),\qquad
 V:=\operatorname{span}\{u_c:c\in\mathcal T\},\qquad
 B_*:=D_*\cap V.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus \(V\) is two-dimensional and \(B_*\) is an origin-symmetric two-dimensional convex body in \(V\). Define the finite residual target measure
\[
 \mu_I:=\sum_{c\in\mathcal T}T_c\,\delta_{u_c}.
\tag{11}
\]
Then every \(w\in V\) satisfies
\[
 \boxed{\mu_I\!\left(w+\frac12B_*\right)\le G.}
\tag{12}
\]
Consequently, for every integer \(N\ge1\) and every \(w_1,\ldots,w_N\in V\),
\[
 \boxed{
 \mu_I\!\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^N
 \left(w_i+\frac12B_*\right)\right)\le NG.}
\tag{13}
\]
In particular, if
\[
 \{u_c:c\in\mathcal T\}
 \subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^N\left(w_i+\frac12B_*\right),
\tag{14}
\]
then \(G\ge\Theta_I/N\).

Let
\[
 \gamma_d:=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d,
 \qquad
 N_d:=\left\lfloor\frac{3}{1-2\gamma_d}\right\rfloor.
\tag{15}
\]
Condition (9) implies \(d\ge2\), so \(1-2\gamma_d>0\). If (14) holds with \(N\le N_d\), then
\[
 \boxed{
 \mathcal A(C)
 \ge\left(\frac1N+\frac{2\gamma_d}{3}\right)\Theta_I
 \ge\frac{\Theta_I}{3}
 >\frac Q{100}.}
\tag{16}
\]
Hence no configuration satisfying the hard inequality (1) can have such a cover. The integer \(N_d\) is the largest \(N\) for which the lower bound in (16), using only \(G\), \(R_{\mathrm{sel}}(C)\), and \(D\), reaches \(\Theta_I/3\). This theorem does not assert that the accepted hypotheses supply any uniformly bounded residual-cell cover.
